correctness.rationale: The exact block loss difference is half the squared head Gram residual plus ||YZ^T||_F^2-||Z||_F^2+||ZZ^T||_F^2/2. The gradient vanishes at each collapsed orientation, and k+1 columns suffice for exact fit by disjoint supports. If the minimum head entry is strictly above 1/sqrt(m), it remains so in a neighborhood; nonnegative rows z give ||Yz^T||_2^2 >= m(min Y_ij)^2||z||_2^2. This proves local optimality for all feasible perturbations there, with nonstrictness from nearby positive unit orientations. Below threshold, inserting one entry t in a minimizing column of one tail row gives a negative quadratic coefficient and a positive t^4/2; head scaling also supplies an increasing direction. At equality the displayed Hessian coefficient is nonnegative on the full tangent cone (head arbitrary, tail nonnegative, gradient zero). Reducing the minimizing squared orientation coordinate by t^2/m and transferring that mass to another coordinate keeps the head Gram fixed; the same tail insertion now gives exactly -t^4/2 at distance t+O(t^3). The critical construction needs r>=2; the stronger r>=k+1 hypothesis ensures zero global loss. The balanced vector uniquely maximizes the minimum coordinate, so a local minimum in this family exists exactly for m>r. The source's exact-rational checks are finite; its script was inspected, not executed.
